title: Towards Knowledge-Grounded Counter Narrative Generation for Hate Speech
measurement_description: The paper evaluates the capability of Language Models to generate knowledge-grounded counter-narratives in response to online hate speech. Specifically, it measures the novelty, diversity, suitableness, informativeness, and intra-coherence of the generated responses, primarily focusing on hate speech targeting religious groups such as Islamophobia (in-domain) and Antisemitism (cross-domain zero-shot testing).
findings: Injecting external knowledge into pre-trained large language models (specifically GPT-2 variants) significantly improved the generation of informative and suitable counter-narratives against religious hate speech (Islamophobia and Antisemitism). GPT-2 fine-tuned with knowledge (GPT-2_KN) produced the most suitable and informative responses according to expert human evaluators, successfully contradicting extreme statements with fact-bound arguments, whereas XNLG suffered from excessively copying the source knowledge.
